entries.title: Marginalia is open to everyone
entries.body: Marginalia, the annotations mode, no longer needs the Experimental features switch, and signed-out visitors reading a shared article can use it too. When you add an article, its groundwork is queued with the other main modes, unless automatic modes are turned off. The first time you open an article in a browser while signed in, Marginalia appears alongside Summary where both fit; a view you saved still takes precedence.

entries.title: Each article in your library shows its topics
entries.body: When you are signed in, every article in your library carries its topics: all of them when there are four or fewer, otherwise the first three and a count of the rest. The labels are for reading, not clicking, and in the table view they appear as plain text.

entries.title: Links to public articles carry a preview image
entries.body: A link to a public article now comes with a Spideryarn image and asks for the large preview card on Twitter. The preview title can add the authors from the article's byline (one name, two, or the first and "et al.") when the whole title fits the length limit. Search engines are still asked not to index the pages.

entries.title: Quote highlights are stronger in the dark appearance
entries.body: Highlighted quotes in the article are filled more strongly when you read in the dark appearance, where they were hard to see against the background. The colour itself is unchanged, and the light appearance is as it was.

entries.title: The command bar's ask is a button
entries.body: When nothing matched what you typed, the command bar told you to press Enter to ask what you meant, which could not be done when dictating on an iPhone. There is an "Ask what you meant" button instead. After an ask that fails it reads "Try again", and a sentence that is too long gets its own message.
